title: br and tr blends
parentNote: Two new blends today, and they are a pair: br and tr. Your child has met fr already, so the r on the end is familiar — the difference is what the tongue does. For l blends the tongue tip flicks up and touches behind the teeth; for r blends it pulls back and touches nothing at all, so brush and blush are the pair to keep side by side. The usual slip is a little vowel creeping in, so brick comes out "buh-rick" — say the b and the r on their own, slowly, then run them together with nothing between. One thing not to correct: tr really does sound like "chr" in ordinary speech, so a child who says "chruck" for truck has heard it right. Say it your normal way and let them copy that, not a stiff t-then-r.

activities.mouthCue: Pop your lips shut for the b, then pull your tongue back for the r so it touches nothing.
activities.prompt: Two letters, two sounds, said in a hurry. No little vowel in the middle.

activities.mouthCue: Tap your tongue behind your teeth for the t, then pull it straight back for the r.
activities.prompt: Say it fast, the way you say it in truck. It comes out a bit like chr, and that is right.
All three start with your lips. Find the one where your tongue pulls back.
These all end with an r. Listen to the very first sound.
Say the b and the r on their own first, then push them together.
Same again with the other one. Say the t and the r, then run them into each other.
Now keep br in one piece. Three sounds: br, i, ck.
A blend on the front and a blend on the back.
Same ending. One starts at your lips and one starts behind your teeth.
Both start with a b. Does the tongue flick up to the teeth, or pull back?
All three start with tr. The middle sound decides it.

activities.text: A big truck did tip and a brick fell on the track.
Ted trod on a brick and did a big hop!
Is the red brush up on the shelf with the bricks?

activities.title: The brick truck
activities.prompt: Read the story one line at a time. Tap any word you want to hear again.
lines: Ted got a red truck and Jen got ten red bricks.
They did stack the bricks up on the back and set off.
Jen did tug the truck up the hill and it did tip on a rock!
The bricks fell off and did land in the mud with a thud.
Ted did brush the mud off and did grin. It is a mud truck!
